chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal, Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them), said: 'The cost of living in this world has become severe, and the cost of living in the Hereafter [is also severe]. As for the cost of this world, you do not extend your hand to anything from it except that you find a prodigal who has preceded you to it; and as for the cost of the Hereafter, you do not find helpers to assist you in it.'

key_terms.فَاجِرًا: Prodigal / wicked person / one who spends lavishly or competes fiercely

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the difficulty of worldly sustenance and the Hereafter according to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (AS) highlights the competitive scarcity of worldly provision, where the prodigal often seize opportunities, contrasting it with the spiritual isolation of the Hereafter where no one can assist in bearing the 'cost' of one's deeds. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on self-reliance in worship and the transient nature of material gain versus the enduring weight of individual accountability. The metaphor of 'ma'unah' (sustenance/cost) underscores the economic and spiritual realities of the believer's journey.
